## Accessibility Issue: Form validation error not announced to screen readers (WCAG 4.1.3) **Bug ID:** `A11Y-d8b2e6f1` (instance) / `A11Y-c7a9d5e3` (pattern) **URL:** https://give.example.org/donate **XPath:** `//div[contains(@class,'form-error')]` **Full DOM path:** `/html/body/main[@id='main-content']/section[@class='donation-form-section']/form[@id='donation-form']/div[contains(@class,'form-error')]` **WCAG SC:** 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA) **Rule:** Manual testing — Screen reader announcement of dynamic content **Severity:** High **Frequency:** 1 instance on this page; appears whenever form validation fails with an empty amount field ### HTML Snippet ```html
Please enter a donation amount.
``` ### Description When the donation form is submitted with an empty "amount" field, a visual error message appears in red above the form. However, VoiceOver on macOS does not announce this dynamically inserted content at all. A blind user receives no auditory feedback that submission failed — they simply hear nothing and may assume their action had no effect or succeeded silently. The root cause is that the error `
` is a plain container with no ARIA attributes to signal it as a status message (`role="alert"`, `aria-live`, etc.). Additionally, the input field itself receives no programmatic indication of an error (no `aria-invalid="true"`), and there is no association between the error text and the form control via `aria-describedby`. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://give.example.org/donate in Safari 17.4 on macOS 14 2. Ensure VoiceOver is running (`Cmd + F5` or from System Settings) 3. Leave the "Donation Amount" field (`#donation-amount`) empty 4. Press Enter or click the submit button to attempt form submission 5. Listen carefully — no error message will be announced by VoiceOver 6. Manually navigate (using `VO + Right Arrow`) back toward the top of the form to discover the visual-only error message ### Expected Behaviour When the form is submitted with an empty required field: - VoiceOver should immediately announce something like "Error: Please enter a donation amount." - The input field should be programmatically marked as invalid (`aria-invalid="true"`) - Focus may optionally move to the first errored field or the error message itself ### Actual Behaviour VoiceOver announces nothing upon failed submission. No audible indication of an error occurs unless the user manually navigates back to the top of the form where they might visually (if sighted) notice the red text — but even then, it is not linked programmatically to the input field. ### Testing Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Browser | Safari 17.4 | | OS | macOS 14 Sonoma | | Screen reader | VoiceOver (built-in) | | Testing tool | Manual testing only — no automated scan performed | ### Impact **Blind users relying on screen readers are completely unaware that their form submission failed.** They receive zero feedback and may repeatedly attempt to submit the same incomplete form, believing it worked or was ignored. This creates confusion, frustration, and potentially causes them to abandon the donation process entirely during a critical campaign period. Sighted users see the red error text immediately; non-sighted users get silence — an inequitable experience that violates core principles of accessible design. ### Suggested Fix (optional) ```html
Please enter a donation amount.
Please enter a donation amount.
``` Additionally, consider moving keyboard focus to the first error message or errored input field after submission so users are directed straight to where action is needed.
